newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank of Queensland sees lower 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank of Queensland sees lower 2nd half.

text.p: Regional bank Bank of Queensland said on Tuesday it expected its profit for the second half of the 1996/97 year to end-August would be below its profit for the first half.
Bank of Queensland reported a first half net profit to February 28 of A$7.995 million.

As a result, the final dividend would not match the 16 cents a share paid in the second half of 1995/96, but was expected to at least match the 12 cents a share paid in the first half of 1996/97, the bank said.

Factors reducing profitability included margin reductions of more than 1.50 percentage points on most housing loans, recent easings in official interest rates, and costs linked to investments in longer-term profitability arising from a strategic review last year.
The bank said it continued to have strong asset growth, while lending volumes in May reached record levels.
"This strong growth will flow through to profit in future periods," it said.
Bank of Queensland shares closed down eight cents at A$5.42.
